subject: Whether a $5,200.00 remittance asserted to have been wired on December 19, 2023 was applied to the account
amount_claimed_by_servicer: n/a - the servicer asserts nothing about $5,200.00
computation_shown: No single entry of $5,200.00 exists anywhere in the 72-row ledger. The only candidate is the 12/21/23 cluster, two days after the asserted wire date. Three defensible readings of that cluster: (i) PAYMENT ENTRIES ONLY: $2,081.81 + $2,082.46 + $191.60 = $4,355.87; variance vs $5,200.00 = $844.13. (ii) ALL POSITIVE ENTRIES including the [COL?] late-charge waive: $2,081.81 + $2,082.46 + $191.60 + $729.13 = $5,085.00; variance = $115.00. (iii) NET OF ALL FIVE ROWS including the -$104.12 late-charge assessment: $4,980.88; variance = $219.12. NONE equals $5,200.00.
assumptions: (1) The December 19, 2023 wire date is an input supplied by the client and is NOT established by any source in this manifest. (2) Reading (ii) uses the $729.13 Late Charge Waive, which is marked [COL?] at TXN-033 and is therefore shown for completeness only and is NOT relied on. (3) A two-day lag between wire and posting is ordinary but is an assumption, not a fact of record.
competing_computation: All three readings are set out above rather than one being chosen.
what_would_resolve: The wire confirmation or MT-103 from the sending bank showing amount, date and beneficiary; and the servicer's cash-application record for 12/19-12/21/2023.
notes: MATERIAL CORRECTION TO THE PHASE 1 FINDING. Phase 1 reported that no $5,200.00 entry exists, which remains literally true. With the December 19, 2023 date now supplied, the 12/21/23 cluster is a plausible candidate that Phase 1 did not evaluate. The honest position is neither 'the payment is absent' nor 'the payment was applied': the cluster is close in time and NOT equal in amount, and the difference is unexplained on this record. NOTE ALSO that SRC-021, the later 16-count pleading, contains NO $5,200.00 allegation at all.

subject: Whether the September 2023 reinstatement credit fully distributed

(2) The offsetting Unapplied Payment rows in the same cluster are bookkeeping counterparts and are not additional money. Both assumptions are drawn from the cluster's structure, not stated by the document. Several rows in the cluster are [COL?] (TXN-024).
competing_computation: If the $729.13 principal-only entry is NOT part of this distribution, the applied total is $18,789.75 and the residual is $799.13.

subject: Four 2025 trial payments totalling $7,598.24; none applied to principal or interest
amount_claimed_by_servicer: Three of four reversed with NSF Fee Assessments
amount_supported_by_records: $1,899.56 retained in suspense and never applied
computation_shown: Four tenders of $1,899.56 = $7,598.24 total. Reversed: 05/02 (by 05/08), 05/10 (by 05/15), 06/18 (by 06/25) = $5,698.68. NOT reversed: 05/17/25 = $1,899.56. Ledger 'Ending Unapplied Balance' at the 03/10/26 print = $1,899.56, which MATCHES the unreversed tender exactly. Amount applied to principal or interest from any of the four: $0.00. Principal balance throughout: $140,288.02, unchanged.
assumptions: (1) The three NSF Fee Assessment rows relate to the three reversals they are dated with. (2) No later print shows this balance applied.
competing_computation: n/a - the ending balance is stated on the face of the document and matches.
what_would_resolve: Plaintiffs' depositary records for each of the four tenders, showing whether any was returned; and Shellpoint's suspense policy and TPP terms.
notes: THE STRONGEST DOCUMENTED PAYMENT FACT IN THE MATTER, and it comes from the defendants' own record. CONTRARY POINT, stated plainly: three of the four were reversed with NSF entries, which on the ledger's face is a complete explanation for their non-application. Only the 05/17/25 tender is unexplained, and it is worth more than the other three combined. Each NSF Fee Assessment is recorded in the amount of $0.00 - an oddity worth a question, not a conclusion. SRC-021 P29 pleads these were TPP payments and that Plaintiffs' bank records show none was returned; that document is not in the manifest.

computation_shown: 09/26/23 Unapplied Payment +$855.00: unapplied balance $0.00 -> $855.00. 10/11/23 Unapplied Payment -$855.00: unapplied balance $855.00 -> $0.00. No Regular Payment, Principal Only Payment, or fee application in the amount of $855.00 appears on or near 10/11/23. Principal unchanged at $142,095.76 across both rows.
assumptions: (1) The two entries are a pair. (2) The ledger would show an application if one had occurred, as it does elsewhere.

Attributing it to Shellpoint, which did not board the loan until 07/07/24, is contradicted by the ledger's own 'PriorServicer' money-type marker on both rows.

subject: Fees charged to the account while principal never moved
computation_shown: SLS-era assessments, 4 entries 05/06/24-06/11/24: $30.00 + $175.00 + $570.00 + $665.00 = $1,440.00. Shellpoint-era disbursements, 23 entries 08/12/24-02/27/26: $6,968.74. Total 27 entries = $8,408.74. Principal balance on the first of those rows: $140,288.02. On the last: $140,288.02. Change: $0.00.
assumptions: (1) Every row whose description contains FC Costs, Attorney Cost, Certified Mail, BPO/Aprsl, Title Cost or Property Inspection is a default or foreclosure charge. (2) No fee was later refunded outside the visible period.
competing_computation: Restricting to the window pleaded at SRC-021 P32 (07/19/2024-01/13/2026) yields 20 entries totalling $5,394.13 - which still exceeds the '$3,500' and 'fifteen' pleaded.
what_would_resolve: The security deed and note provisions authorising each fee type; the servicer's fee schedule; and the invoices behind each disbursement.
notes: The AMOUNTS are not in dispute - they are the servicer's own figures and they foot. What is disputed is whether they were authorised, which is a contract and regulation question and NOT an accounting one. Recorded as characterization-dispute for that reason. The ledger corroborates SRC-021 P32 and exceeds it.

subject: Two prints of the same Loan History Statement bearing different dates
computation_shown: SRC-024 bears a print timestamp OCR'd as 'OV16/2026 4:29:59PM' = 01/16/2026 4:29:59PM, matching the date the Witt Letter enclosed a ledger. SRC-013/SRC-006 bears a print timestamp of 03/10/2026 12:57:58PM. The 03/02/2026 CFPB response (SRC-012) lists 'payment history' among its enclosures but predates the 03/10/2026 print by eight days. At least two, and possibly three, distinct prints are implicated.
assumptions: (1) The OCR reading 'OV16' is 01/16. (2) SRC-024 is page 3 of the same five-page statement.
what_would_resolve: Production of every print of the account history the servicer generated, with generation dates, and the as-mailed enclosure to the 03/02/2026 letter.
notes: Comparing prints of the same statement is the cheapest available test for whether entries changed between generations. The overlapping rows of SRC-024 and SRC-013 were compared and no substantive difference was found - only OCR degradation in SRC-024. That is a NEGATIVE result and is reported as such. Only one page overlaps, so the test is far from complete.
